trafficCapture.title: Traffic capture
trafficCapture.description:
When enabled, every agent's HTTP traffic is stored in full through the recording proxy, and agents are injected with the traffic_search / traffic_get tools and proxy configuration (the prompt includes proxy notes).

When off (default) no traffic is recorded: the agent does not receive proxy configuration or traffic tools, and the prompt contains no proxy-related content. Agents are rebuilt immediately after switching.
trafficCapture.labelOn: On · recording traffic and injecting proxy
trafficCapture.labelOff: Off · no recording, no proxy injection

agentBinding.title: Automatic agent traffic binding
agentBinding.description:
Off by default. When enabled, the report agent triggered on vulnerability creation reviews existing HTTP requests/responses and links the matching traffic before writing the report. Reading packets and the extra tool calls increase token consumption.

Reporting still works for TCP, uncaptured traffic, or when no traffic matches. This switch does not affect traffic capture, manual binding, or viewing saved evidence. It takes effect for the next round of agents; once disabled, new automatic bindings are rejected immediately.

globalProxy.title: Global proxy
globalProxy.description:
All agents' target traffic egresses through this proxy (hide the source IP / use a jump host). Supports http / https / socks5, optionally with user:pass authentication. Empty = direct connection.

With traffic capture on, it acts as the recording proxy's upstream (traffic is still stored in full, then egresses through this proxy); with capture off, it is injected directly into the agent's bash / WebFetch egress. Independent of the web search proxy and the LLM proxy.

Note: with capture off, socks5 relies on each CLI tool honoring ALL_PROXY (curl works; some tools may ignore it). If you mainly use socks5, enable traffic capture — on that path the MITM does the dialing itself, invisible to tools and reliably effective.
globalProxy.statusConfigured: Configured · all target traffic egresses through this proxy
globalProxy.statusNotConfigured: Not configured · target traffic egresses directly

constraints.title: Operation constraint injection
constraints.description:
When enabled, each task's operation constraints (the allow/deny entries maintained under "Operation constraints" in the task overview) are spliced into the corresponding agent's system prompt to bound the exploration scope (e.g. "only test the current port", "no brute forcing").

You can control injection into the planner and the worker separately; both are on by default. Switching takes effect immediately (read on the next turn) without rebuilding agents. When off, the agent no longer sees the constraints.

experimental.title: Experimental features
experimental.description:
Mechanisms still being validated, off by default. They may change agent behavior or affect stability; enable only after understanding the impact.

noa context compaction: the model actively compacts long conversation history (norma v0.4.0). When enabled, the four agent types integrated into the platform (planner / worker / main agent / chat) switch to noa-managed context in place of the built-in compaction, and the pre-compaction originals are archived under the task working directory for later review. Switching takes effect immediately (for runs started afterwards) without rebuilding agents; when disabled, the built-in compaction is restored immediately.

webSearch.title: Web search
webSearch.description:
This is the web search master switch + source config. Only when it is enabled can each agent's config separately choose whether to enable web_search (returns only titles/links/snippets without fetching bodies; fetching is handled by WebFetch). Web search does not go through the recording proxy and is independent of traffic capture.

Sources: DuckDuckGo (ddgs) (no key needed), Brave (free tier) (requires a Brave API Key), Tavily (requires a Tavily API Key) or DeepSeek (reuses the current LLM config). When the master switch is off, the per-agent web search switches are unavailable.
webSearch.labelOn: Master switch on · can be enabled per agent config
webSearch.labelOff: Off · agents cannot enable web search

deepseek.heading: DeepSeek official web search
deepseek.note1: This source directly reuses the currently active LLM config. It therefore supports official DeepSeek models only, and that config must use the anthropic protocol — DeepSeek's OpenAI-protocol endpoint does not support server-side search. This source may stop working after switching LLM configs.
deepseek.note2: Unlike other sources, the search runs server-side on DeepSeek: each search consumes an extra model call (incurring token costs), search requests do not go through the egress proxy above and are not recorded as traffic; results contain titles and links only (no snippets); use WebFetch when you need the page body.
deepseek.note3: Verify these conditions yourself; the system does not block on them. Use the "Test search" button below to run a real search and check.

brave.needsKey: Brave is selected but no key is configured — the search tool stays disabled until you save one.
brave.help: The free tier allows about 2,000 queries/month. Get a key at https://brave.com/search/api/.

tavily.needsKey: Tavily is selected but no key is configured — the search tool stays disabled until you save one.
tavily.help: Register and get an API key at https://tavily.com.

keenable.placeholder: Optional: leave empty for the keyless endpoint
keenable.help: Queries leave this instance and go to api.keenable.ai. The request carries X-Keenable-Title: ARTEX so the provider can identify the caller. With no key, the public endpoint is rate-limited per IP; a key raises the limit, but the backend works without one.

egressProxy.label: Egress proxy (optional)
egressProxy.help: A dedicated egress proxy used only to reach search endpoints (VPN/SOCKS etc.). Unrelated to the traffic-recording MITM proxy; use it to reach endpoints when the network is blocked.

test.hint: Run a real "test" search with the current config (source + proxy + key) to verify it works.

python.title: Custom scripts · Python interpreter
python.description: Custom script tools run Python with it. Auto-detected at startup (python3 first); you can enter an absolute path to a venv / specific version here; leave empty to auto-detect at runtime.

concurrency.title: Work concurrency · worker agent count
concurrency.description: The number of worker agents running concurrently per task (default 3). Higher values mean more parallel probing and higher consumption. Changes apply to tasks started afterwards; running tasks are unaffected.

chatSend.title: Chat input send key binding
chatSend.description:
Shared by the main-agent chat inputs on the chat page and task details; takes effect immediately on selection, no saving needed.

This preference lives only in this browser, does not sync with the account, and must be set again after switching browsers or clearing site data.
chatSend.label: Send mode

options.enter: Enter to send, Shift+Enter for newline
options.ctrl-enter: Ctrl+Enter to send, Enter for newline

noiseProfile.title: Target noise
noiseProfile.description: Paces the requests ARTEX itself sends to targets (WebFetch, http custom tools, the enrich probe) and sets the low-and-slow guidance in agent prompts. With traffic capture on, Bash commands that use the proxy (curl, wget, python-requests…) are paced too, by rate and jitter only: the in-flight, cache and retry limits apply to ARTEX's own requests. Raw scanners such as nmap, and commands that bypass the proxy, are not paced; this is best effort, not a security boundary. This setting takes precedence over ARTEX_NOISE_PROFILE and applies to the next request.

off.label: Off
off.limits: Off: requests and their timing are unchanged, and nothing is counted.

quiet.label: Quiet
quiet.limits: 2 req/s per host (burst 4), 1 in flight per host, 8 overall, jitter up to 250 ms, identical GETs of a task cached 60 s, up to 3 retries on 429/503.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.limits: 5 req/s per host (burst 10), 2 in flight per host, 16 overall, jitter up to 40 ms, identical GETs of a task cached 30 s, up to 3 retries on 429/503.

aggressive.label: Aggressive
aggressive.limits: 20 req/s per host (burst 40), 4 in flight per host, 32 overall, jitter up to 5 ms, identical GETs of a task cached 10 s, up to 2 retries on 429/503.
